text: Every partition lives on disk on one broker, but Kafka never keeps just one copy. Replication factor tells Kafka how many total copies of each partition to keep, across different brokers.
Only the leader serves reads and writes. Followers replicate from the leader. A follower fully caught up is an in-sync replica, or ISR; a lagging one drops out of that set until it catches up.

min.insync.replicas decides how many replicas a write has to reach before it's acknowledged. Losing one broker stays safe; losing too many at once, Kafka refuses new writes rather than risk data loss.
When a leader dies: the broker stops responding, the controller notices the missed session timeout, a new leader is elected from the ISR set with zero data loss, and clients reconnect automatically.
Replication turns a dead broker into a non-event, as long as min.insync.replicas was set honestly. Next up: partitioning strategy.
